summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic rectal adenocarcinoma and sickle cell disease presented with URI symptoms and developed a life-threatening reaction to Zosyn infusion, resulting in cardiac arrest and requiring two minutes of CPR. She was stabilized, transferred to the ICU, and later to the medicine floor. She received a blood transfusion for anemia, and her platelets, which dropped acutely post-arrest, improved over the hospitalization. Her infection was treated with antibiotics, transitioning from IV cefepime/azithromycin to oral levofloxacin. Pain from sickle cell crisis and post-CPR sternal tenderness was managed with IV and oral opioids. She recovered well, with stable vital signs and improving labs, and was discharged home with visiting nurse services, a plan to complete antibiotics, and follow-up appointments including allergy testing.
